tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

1	# ERN — Vérification exploratoire : dérivabilité des arènes et faisabilité de `DataStack`
2	
3	Branche `formal/derivability_0.1`, créée depuis `formal/validation_0.1`. Brouillon : pas de fusion, pas de PR. Spécification de référence : `ERN_Spec1_Memory_Model_specification_normative_candidate_corrigee.md` (Spec 1 candidate, non validée, non copiée dans le dépôt). Les modules existants (`Ern/MM02.lean`, `Ern/MM03.lean`, `Ern/MM23.lean`, `Ern/HandlePool.lean`, `Ern/MM03/Horrors.lean`, `Ern/MM23/Horrors.lean`, `Ern/MM03/LockOptions.lean`) sont inchangés. Nouveaux modules : `Ern/Derived/Arena.lean` (question 1), `Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (question 2).
4	
5	## État de vérification
6	
7	| Étape | Commit | Module |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Question 1 | 6b7cf20 | `Ern/Derived/Arena.lean` |
10	| Question 2 | 59c276f | `Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` |
11	| Revue adverse, corrections, rapport | voir l'historique de la branche | les deux modules et ce rapport |
12	
13	- `lake build` : réussi, sans avertissement.
14	- La recherche de `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide` et `axiom` est vide ; aucun `noncomputable`.
15	- Parcours `collectAxioms` de **toutes** les constantes des deux modules : rien hors de `propext` et `Quot.sound` (pas même `Classical.choice`).
16	  - `Derived.Arena` : 159 constantes, dont 86 théorèmes ;
17	  - `Lib.DataStack` : 360 constantes, dont 156 théorèmes.
18	
19	**Passages de la spécification lus et formalisés.** §36, §42 à §47, §54 à §58, §60 (O1), §61 (O2), §62 (O3), §65 (O8), §76 (O17), §77 (O18), §78 (O19), §86, §88, §89. Chaque définition et théorème cite son passage dans sa docstring.
20	
21	**Méthode.** Les équivalences sont énoncées pour tout état atteint (`Reachable k statics s`, sous `DDSound k`) et prouvées dans les deux sens ; chaque écart est accompagné d'un contre-exemple sur un état atteint, décidé par `decide`. Les contre-exemples sont conservés comme théorèmes `ce_*`.
22	
23	**Objets comparés.** Le noyau (`Ern.MM03`) formalise un texte antérieur ; `issue` et `reset` y diffèrent de la Spec 1 candidate. Le module définit donc les opérations restreintes à partir du texte candidat :
24	
25	- `MetaRightM` : `MetaRight` réduit à sa première branche (`Modify` exerçable sur la valeur arène), conformément à l'hypothèse de la tâche ;
26	- `IssueR` : §77 avec `MetaRightM`, sur une entrée donnée.
27	  - Il reprend les clauses statiques du noyau (`issueStaticR_iff`).
28	  - Il y ajoute deux points du texte candidat absents du noyau : la destination hors de la région (§77.2, « prévention locale de l'auto-blocage ») et l'ancre du bloc ajoutée à `D(destination)` (§77, effet : « qui reçoit l'ancre correspondante »).
29	  - `ArrivalR` regroupe les contrôles sur l'état d'arrivée : `AnchorOrder` de la nouvelle ancre (§77.3) et `AnchorOrderHeld` (§77.6).
30	  - `IssueAtR` ajoute la recherche de l'entrée dans l'état (§77.1, « L'entrée `arena` existe ») et réécrit ses métadonnées, comme `IssueAt` du noyau.
31	  - La disponibilité est le `Avail` du noyau, lu feuille par feuille ; c'est une ambiguïté du texte, voir (c) 8 et (f) 2.
32	- `ResetPreR` : §78 avec `MetaRightM`. Il comprend la vivacité de l'entrée (§78.1) et reprend les clauses de `ResetAtPre` et `ResetPre` du noyau (`resetPreR_iff`). `ResetAtPreR` ajoute la recherche de l'entrée.
33	
34	## (a) Statut de `issue_as_kernel`, `reset_as_kernel`, `newArena_as_library`
35	
36	### `issue_as_kernel` — prouvé, avec deux clauses d'écart identifiées
37	
38	Séquence noyau : `split` de `internal` sur `[région]` (O2 à une région, c'est-à-dire une dérivation `Modify` sur une liste de feuilles), puis `store` (O8) du bloc dans la destination. Lorsque la région est l'empreinte d'un emplacement `q`, `split` coïncide avec `derive` (O1) de `internal` sur `q`, avec le même effet (`derive_iff_split`).
39	
40	| Théorème | Énoncé |
41	|---|---|
42	| `issue_to_seq` | `IssueR … (ok s' ar')` et `HasRight s' Modify dst` ⟹ `split` puis `store` sont `ok`, avec l'état d'arrivée `s'` |
43	| `seq_to_issue` | `split` puis `store` `ok`, région disponible, destination non `Init` ⟹ `IssueR … (ok s₂ _)`, même état d'arrivée |
44	| `issue_as_kernel_split` | équivalence des deux, pour toute région |
45	| `issue_as_kernel` | même équivalence avec `derive` sur un emplacement `q` (région = empreinte de `q`) |
46	| `issueR_fail_iff`, `issueR_reject_iff`, `issueR_total`, `issueR_det` | `fail` ⟺ clauses statiques et région indisponible (§77.4) ; `reject` ⟺ ni `ok` ni `fail` |
47	
48	Forme exacte (`issue_as_kernel_split`), pour tout état atteint `s` et toute entrée `ar ∈ s.arenas` :
49	
50	```
51	IssueR ar r dst s (ok s' ar') ∧ HasRight s' Modify dst
52	  ⟺ Avail ar r ∧ (dst non Init) ∧ split(internal, [r]) ok ∧ store(bloc, dst) ok vers s' ∧ ar' = métadonnées de §77
53	```
54	
55	- **État d'arrivée.** La partie noyau de l'état d'arrivée de `issue` (avec l'ancre ajoutée à `D(dst)` par le texte candidat) est l'état d'arrivée de `store`. C'est une égalité de structures (`issueEffR_eq`), pas une simple correspondance.
56	- **Clauses qui coïncident.**
57	  - `MetaRightM` est exactement l'exercice de `internal` en `Modify` exigé par O1.1 et O2.1 (`metaRightM_iff`).
58	  - Le droit effectif de §77.5 est celui de O1.2 et O2.1.
59	  - La destination hors région (§77.2) est la première moitié de O8.3.
60	  - Les contrôles d'arrivée de §77.3 et §77.6 sont ceux de O8.4 et O8.5 (`AnchorOrderHeld`). `AnchorOrderHeld` ne dépend pas de `D`.
61	  - La seconde moitié de O8.3 (stockage possédé transitivement par la destination) n'introduit **aucun** rejet de plus dans un état atteint. Une destination qui posséderait un emplacement utilisable détiendrait l'autorité racine de cet emplacement (`RootLive`), ce que §77.2 exclut déjà (`ownedIn_holds`).
62	- **Clauses qui diffèrent** : voir (c), écarts 1 et 2.
63	- **Disponibilité.** Une région émise puis libérée sans `reset` est indisponible dans les métadonnées, mais `internal` y a retrouvé son droit effectif. `issue` y échoue (`fail`) alors que la séquence est `ok` (`ce_avail`). C'est le rôle attendu des métadonnées : `fail` ⟺ clauses statiques ∧ région indisponible.

65	### `reset_as_kernel` — prouvé, avec deux clauses d'écart ; la seconde clause ne découle pas de `release`
66	
67	Séquence noyau : `derive` de `internal` en `Modify` sur le stockage (O1), puis `release` (O3) de l'autorité dérivée.
68	
69	| Théorème | Énoncé |
70	|---|---|
71	| `reset_to_seq` | `ResetPreR` (entrée vivante comprise) ⟹ `derive` puis `release` `ok` |
72	| `seq_to_reset` | `derive` puis `release` `ok`, aucune dérivation active d'empreinte vide, `internal` ancre d'aucun emplacement utilisable ⟹ `ResetPreR` |
73	| `reset_as_kernel` | équivalence des deux |
74	| `reset_seq_arrival` | l'état d'arrivée de la séquence est l'état de départ plus une autorité inactive ; `reset` ne change pas la partie noyau |
75	| `reset_clause3_strict` | sous la lecture stricte de §78.3, la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 |

77	Provenance des clauses de `ResetPre` :
78	
79	- **§78.1.** `MetaRightM` est l'exercice exigé par O1.1 (`metaRightM_iff`).
80	- **§78.2** (« aucune autorité dérivée de `internal` ne reste active »). Elle découle de O1.2 (droit effectif `Modify` sur tout le stockage) pour toute dérivation qui couvre une feuille. Une dérivation active d'**empreinte vide** (`split` de `internal` sur `[[]]`) bloque `reset` sans bloquer la séquence (`ce_reset_empty`).
81	- **§78.3.** Elle **ne découle pas** des préconditions de `release`. `release` d'une autorité fraîche ne contrôle que ses propres ancres (O3.3), et la séquence ne libère que cette autorité fraîche.
82	  - Pour les dérivées strictes de `internal`, la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 : une ancre d'un emplacement utilisable est active (`reset_clause3_strict`).
83	  - Pour `internal` lui-même, elle ne découle de rien. Le noyau lit « sous-arbre d'origines de `internal` » en y incluant `internal`. Une valeur arène qui a reçu `internal` par `store` porte `internal` dans `D` (O8, effet). `reset` y est alors rejeté tant que la valeur arène est utilisable, et la séquence est `ok` (`ce_reset_anchor`, `reset_blocked_by_stored_internal`).

85	### `newArena_as_library` — prouvé : aucune propriété de sûreté ne dépend de la garde
86	
87	- **Inscription.** Elle ne touche aucune composante du noyau (`newArena_kernel_noop`).
88	- **Atteignabilité sans garde.** `ReachableNG` contient tous les pas de `Reachable` plus l'inscription sans la garde de §56 (`NewArenaPreNG`, et `newArenaPre_iff` : la précondition du noyau est `NewArenaPreNG` plus la garde).
89	- **Invariants.** Sur tout état de `ReachableNG`, sous `DDSound`, valent tous les invariants de §57 (`newArena_as_library`) : `WF3`, `Inv3` (I1 à I4, `AnchorOrder`, `NoDangling`), `AnchorOrderHeld`, `NoOrphan` et `ArenaInv` de chaque arène vivante.
90	  - Preuve : chaque pas de `Reachable` préserve ces invariants **et** `RootLive` sur tout état qui les vérifie (`step_inv57`, reprise des cas de `reachable_invariants`, `reachable_anchorOrderHeld`, `reachable_rootLive`).
91	  - L'inscription sans garde les préserve aussi (`newArenaNG_inv57`). La preuve du noyau, `newArena_preserves`, n'utilise d'ailleurs pas la garde.
92	- **I1.** Il rejette la double émission par deux administrations du même `internal`. Un bloc actif dérivé de `internal` ôte à `internal` le droit effectif sur ses feuilles. Ni l'`issue` du noyau, ni `IssueR`, ni `split` ne passent alors, quelle que soit l'entrée (`issue_blocked_by_block`).
93	  - Exemple : `ce_two_admins`. Deux entrées partagent `internal` 4. L'émission de `[5]` par l'entrée 0 est `ok`. Celle de `[5]` par l'entrée 1 est rejetée, alors que ses métadonnées tiennent 5 pour disponible.
94	- **Seul effet observable de la garde.** Il porte sur le classement des issues : avec deux administrations, une région émise par l'autre donne `reject` au lieu de `fail`. Même avec la garde, les métadonnées ne sont pas exactes. Un cadre qui exerce `internal` peut dériver directement depuis lui, et une région disponible est alors rejetée (`ce_avail_reject`).

140	## (d) Statut des théorèmes de `DataStack`
141	
142	`DataStack` est une instance de bibliothèque. Son état contient l'état du noyau, les piles (stockage, `internal`, cellules ordonnées, sommet, blocs émis, marques vivantes) et le prochain identifiant de marque. Ses opérations n'effectuent que des pas du noyau :
143	
144	| Opération | Pas du noyau | Issues |
145	|---|---|---|
146	| `push` | clauses statiques de l'`issue` restreint (§77.1, §77.2) avant la place, puis `split` et `store` | `fail` sans place |
147	| `rewind` | `split` puis `release` (`reset` dérivé) sur les cellules au-dessus de la marque | `fail` pour une marque non vivante de la pile |
148	| `grow` | clauses statiques (dont `MetaRightM`) avant la place, puis `release` du dernier bloc et `issue` dérivé de même base et de taille plus grande vers la même destination, déjà `Init` | `fail` sans place |
149	| `mark` | aucun (métadonnées) | toujours `ok` |
150	| `newStack` | aucun (inscription) | garde de §56 sur les deux registres |
151	
152	Un `newArena` du noyau consulte aussi le registre des piles (`KGuard`, §56). Tout pas `ok` de la bibliothèque est une suite de pas de `Reachable` (`dexec_reach`, `drun_reach`).
153	
154	| Théorème | Statut | Énoncé |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| `rewind_rejects_live_above` | prouvé | marque vivante, autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvrant une cellule au-dessus de la marque ⟹ `rewind` = `reject` ; réciproque `rewind_ok_no_live_above` |
157	| `mark_no_aba` | prouvé | **toute** marque retirée par `rewind m` (`m` et les marques postérieures de la pile) n'est plus vivante dans aucune pile après toute suite d'opérations, et son `rewind` échoue (`fail`), même quand le sommet revient à sa position. Hypothèse `MarksWF` (marques deux à deux distinctes, nommant leur pile, d'identifiants donnés), établie pour tout état atteint par la bibliothèque (`drun_init_marksWF`) |
158	| `rewind_removes` | prouvé | sous `MarksWF` : après `rewind m`, les marques de la pile sont exactement celles antérieures à `m` ; `m` et les postérieures sont retirées |
159	| `rewind_keeps_older_marks` | prouvé | après `rewind m` : marques = celles antérieures à `m`, sommet = sommet de `m`, autres piles inchangées, initialisation inchangée |
160	| `grow_same_base` | prouvé | dernier bloc de même base, de taille `size + extra`, de même destination enregistrée ; dans l'état d'arrivée, l'autorité nouvelle couvre les cellules depuis la même base et est détenue par cette destination, et l'ancien bloc est inactif ; anciennes cellules préfixe des nouvelles |
161	| `grow_keeps_prefix_init` | prouvé | aucune cellule de l'ancien bloc ne change d'initialisation |
162	| `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` | prouvé, via `Ern.MM23` inchangé | voir ci-dessous |
163	
164	Détail de `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes`. `release` et `split` sont des pas sans pas MM-02 (`NoStep`, K4, dont `r6_noStep` conserve `Repr`). `store` correspond à une écriture de la plage de la destination (`storeOps`, L6). Pour toute disposition `LayoutWF`, cette écriture laisse inchangés les octets **et provenances** (`rangeBytes`) de chaque cellule de l'ancien bloc.
165	
166	Cas (`decide`, chaque exécution étant d'abord établie `ok`) :
167	
168	| Cas | Théorème | Contenu |
169	|---|---|---|
170	| plusieurs piles | `case_stacks` | piles indépendantes ; marque d'une autre pile : `fail` ; garde de §56 sur `newStack` et sur le `newArena` du noyau (que le noyau seul accepterait) |
171	| `rewind` refusé puis accepté | `case_rewind` | refusé tant que le bloc 7 vit, accepté après sa libération |
172	| ABA | `case_aba` | sommet revenu à 2 ; la marque retirée `⟨0, 1, 2⟩` échoue ; la nouvelle `⟨0, 2, 2⟩` est acceptée |
173	| `grow` | `case_grow` | accepté en place ; sans place : `fail` ; bloc qui n'est plus le dernier : `reject` |
174	| cadre | `case_frame` | marque à l'entrée de l'appelé, `push` dans un local ; `rewind` refusé tant que le bloc vit ; après `endUse` du local, `rewind` et `exitFrame` acceptés, pile vide |
175	| lecture de `rewind` | `case_rewind_reading` | une autorité dérivée active couvrant la partie d'une région émise après `m` qui est sous `m` (bloc agrandi) ou au-dessus du sommet courant ne bloque pas `rewind` ; un bloc vide (`push` de taille 0) non plus |
176	| statique avant `fail` | `case_static_before_fail` | sans droit sur la valeur pile, `grow` est rejeté avec ou sans place ; `push` vers une destination `Init`, ou intérieure aux cellules demandées, est rejeté même sans place |
177	| atteignabilité | `cases_reachable` | les états noyau des cas sont atteints |
178	
179	Constat utile pour la question 1 : `grow` réémet dans une destination déjà `Init`, celle du bloc libéré. Il n'est exprimable qu'avec l'`issue` dérivé, `store` acceptant une cible `Init` ; `IssueR` le rejetterait (écart 2). `push`, que la tâche définit par l'`issue` restreint, en suit les clauses statiques ; réalisé par `split` et `store`, il en diffère seulement par O8.5 (écart 1, `issue_as_kernel_split`).

217	6. **`DataStack.push` et `grow`.** La tâche définit `push` par l'`issue` restreint, et `grow` par une émission de même base, sans dire laquelle. C'est un choix sémantique : il change les programmes acceptés.
218	   - `push` suit ici les clauses statiques de l'`issue` restreint : destination non `Init`, hors des cellules demandées, droit sur la valeur pile, tous contrôlés avant la place.
219	   - `grow` utilise l'`issue` dérivé : sa destination est `Init`, et l'`issue` restreint la rejetterait toujours.
220	   - Si la formulation (A) de (e) 2 est retenue, les deux coïncident.
221	7. **`DataStack.rewind`.** « Couvre une région émise après `m` » est lu sur les cellules que `rewind` rend (`above`, du sommet de `m` au sommet courant). Ce n'est pas exactement « les régions émises après `m` » (`case_rewind_reading`) :
222	   - un bloc agrandi après `m` commence sous `m`, et une dérivation active sur sa partie basse ne bloque pas `rewind` ;
223	   - une région émise après `m` puis rendue par un `rewind` intermédiaire est au-dessus du sommet courant ;
224	   - un bloc vide émis après `m` ne bloque pas `rewind`.
225	
226	   Aucun de ces cas ne rend disponible une cellule couverte. Une lecture « couvre la région entière » laisserait `rewind` passer quand une dérivation en couvre une partie seulement, puis rejetterait le `push` suivant (I1). Quelle lecture est voulue ?
227	
228	### Décisions de représentation prises ici (à confirmer)
229	
230	- **`IssueR` suit le texte candidat** : destination hors région, ancre ajoutée à `D(dst)`. L'`issue` du noyau en diffère (écart 7). L'équivalence est donc établie pour le texte candidat ; pour l'`issue` du noyau, l'option 2 manque (`H50_options`, jalon 3).
231	- **Lecture inclusive de §78.3 pour `ResetPreR`**, celle du noyau ((f) 1). **Lecture par feuilles de la disponibilité**, celle du noyau ((f) 2).
232	- **Clauses statiques avant `fail`** (§58), par analogie avec §77 :
233	  - `push` : clauses de `IssueStaticR` (pile vivante, `MetaRightM`, destination feuille utilisable, sous `Modify`, non `Init`, sans autorité active, hors des cellules) ;
234	  - `grow` : `0 < extra`, `b` dernier bloc et au sommet, `b` libérable, pile vivante, `MetaRightM`.
235	
236	  La tâche dit seulement « `fail` si pas de place ». `0 < extra` traduit « taille plus grande ».
237	- **`push` de taille 0** est accepté, comme l'`issue` restreint de la région vide (`ce_empty_region`). Le bloc vide ne bloque aucun `rewind` (`case_rewind_reading`).
238	- **`grow` stocke dans la destination enregistrée** pour le bloc (`Blk.dst`), qui peut ne plus être le détenteur du bloc après un `transfer` (cible `Moved`, permise par §77.2).
239	- **`mark` n'exige aucun droit**, la tâche disant « `mark : ok` ». Il ne modifie que des métadonnées. Une pile inexistante donne `reject`.
240	- **`rewind`** :
241	  - les blocs conservés sont ceux dont la base est sous le sommet de `m` ; un bloc agrandi qui chevauche ce sommet est conservé, et il est nécessairement inactif ;
242	  - une marque est vivante par appartenance à la liste de la pile ;
243	  - une pile inexistante donne `reject`.
244	- **Garde de §56 de `newStack`** : les arènes du noyau et les piles. Les pools de `HandlePool` ne sont pas combinés ici.

36	exercisable `Modify` on the arena value, the holder of `internal` (§46). The `writeShared` branch

38	def MetaRightM (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : Prop :=
39	  OptP (arenaValue s ar) (fun v => HasRight s .modify v) False

51	/-- Static preconditions of the restricted `issue` (candidate Spec 1 §77, clauses 1 and 2, with
52	`MetaRightM`): clause 1, restricted metadata right and `internal` active (the existence of the
53	entry is the lookup of `IssueAtR`; the theorems take an entry `ar ∈ s.arenas`); clause 2, the region
54	within the administered storage, the destination a usable leaf, under exercisable `Modify`, not
55	`Init`, holding no active authority, and not in the region ("Prévention locale de l'auto-blocage",
56	§88). The static restrictions of clause 3 are those of the kernel (`IssueStatic`,
57	`issueStaticR_iff`); its `AnchorOrder` check is on the arrival state (`ArrivalR`). -/
58	def IssueStaticR (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
59	  MetaRightM s ar ∧ s.Active ar.internal ∧ (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal) ∧
60	  s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧
61	  isLeaf s.P dst ∧
62	  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst)
63	    True) ∧
64	  dst ∉ region

66	instance (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
67	    Decidable (IssueStaticR s ar region dst) := by

71	(`IssueStatic`) with the restricted right and the destination outside the region. -/
72	theorem issueStaticR_iff {k : K} {via : Nat} {s : S3} {ar : Arena} {region : List Nat}
73	    {dst : Nat} : IssueStaticR s ar region dst ↔
74	      MetaRightM s ar ∧ IssueStatic k s ar via region dst ∧ dst ∉ region := by
75	  unfold IssueStaticR IssueStatic
76	  exact ⟨fun ⟨h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8⟩ => ⟨h0, ⟨.inl h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7⟩, h8⟩,
77	    fun ⟨h0, ⟨_, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7⟩, h8⟩ => ⟨h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8⟩⟩

85	      D := fun q => if q = dst then s.D dst ++ [s.A.length] else s.D q },

98	/-- The restricted `issue` as a relation (candidate Spec 1 §77; §58): `reject` when a static
99	precondition fails; `fail`, the state unchanged, when the region is not available (§77.4);
100	`reject` when `internal` lacks effective `Modify` on the region (§77.5) or an arrival check fails

108	empty region is always available (`ce_avail_leaf`; report, (f)). -/
109	inductive IssueR (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (s : S3) : IOutcome → Prop where
110	  | ok : IssueStaticR s ar region dst → Avail ar region → IssueRight s ar region →
111	      ArrivalR s ar region dst →
112	      IssueR ar region dst s (.ok (issueEffR s ar region dst).1 (issueEffR s ar region dst).2)
113	  | fail : IssueStaticR s ar region dst → ¬ Avail ar region → IssueR ar region dst s (.fail s ar)
114	  | reject : ¬ IssueStaticR s ar region dst → IssueR ar region dst s .reject
115	  | noRight : IssueStaticR s ar region dst → Avail ar region → ¬ IssueRight s ar region →

117	  | noAnchor : IssueStaticR s ar region dst → Avail ar region → IssueRight s ar region →

123	  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction

127	    ∃ o, IssueR ar region dst s o := by
128	  by_cases h1 : IssueStaticR s ar region dst
129	  · by_cases h2 : Avail ar region
130	    · by_cases h3 : IssueRight s ar region
131	      · by_cases h4 : ArrivalR s ar region dst
132	        · exact ⟨_, .ok h1 h2 h3 h4⟩
133	        · exact ⟨_, .noAnchor h1 h2 h3 h4⟩
134	      · exact ⟨_, .noRight h1 h2 h3⟩
135	    · exact ⟨_, .fail h1 h2⟩

143	  · intro h; cases h with
144	    | ok h1 h2 h3 h4 => exact ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, rfl⟩

155	  · intro h; cases h with

4	/-!
5	# DataStack, a library instance over the kernel (derivability pass 0.1, question 2)
6	
7	A stack administers a storage through an authority `internal` held by the stack value, as an arena
8	does (candidate Spec 1 §36, §46), with library metadata: the ordered leaves of the storage, the
9	top, the issued blocks and the live marks. Its operations are built on kernel steps and on the
10	derived `issue` and `reset` of question 1 (`Ern.Derived.Arena`):
11	
12	* `push`: the restricted `issue` at the top, its static clauses (§77.1, §77.2) checked before the
13	  room, realised by `split` of `internal` on the cells then `store` of the block into the
14	  destination; `fail` when no room is left;
15	* `mark`: a mark (stack, fresh identifier, top), metadata only;
16	* `rewind`: the derived `reset` on the cells above the mark, `split` of `internal` on them then
17	  `release` of the derived authority; `fail` for a mark that is not live in the stack;
18	* `grow`: in place, `release` of the last block, then the derived `issue` of a region of the same
19	  base and of larger size into the same destination, which is `Init`; `fail` when no room is left.
20	
21	Every `ok` step of the library takes kernel steps of `Reachable` only (`dexec_reach`). The theorems
22	of the brief are `rewind_rejects_live_above`, `mark_no_aba` (with `rewind_removes`),
23	`rewind_keeps_older_marks`,
24	`grow_same_base`, `grow_keeps_prefix_init` and `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` (through the refinement
25	`Ern.MM23`, unchanged). The decisions the brief does not settle are listed in the report
26	(`formal/reports/Derivability_v0.1.md`, (c) and (f)).
27	-/
28

31	open Ern.MM03 Ern.HandlePool Ern.MM03.Horrors Ern.Derived.Arena
32	
33	/-- A block issued by a stack: base and size in the cells of the stack, authority, destination. -/
34	structure Blk where
35	  base : Nat
36	  size : Nat
37	  auth : Nat
38	  dst : Nat
39	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
40	
41	/-- A mark (brief: "(pile, identifiant frais, sommet)"). -/
42	structure Mark where
43	  stack : Nat
44	  id : Nat
45	  top : Nat
46	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
47	
48	/-- A stack (brief: "stockage, `internal`, sommet, liste ordonnée des marques vivantes"); `cells`
49	are the ordered leaves of the storage, its footprint at creation; `blocks` the issued blocks,
50	oldest first. The stack value is the holder of `internal`. -/
51	structure Stack where
52	  storage : Nat
53	  internal : Nat
54	  cells : List Nat
55	  top : Nat
56	  blocks : List Blk
57	  marks : List Mark
58	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
59	
60	/-- State of the library: the kernel state, the stacks (the identity of a stack is its index) and
61	the next fresh mark identifier. -/
62	structure DS where
63	  s : S3
64	  stacks : List Stack
65	  fresh : Nat
66	
67	/-- Outcome of a library operation; `fail` leaves the state unchanged (§58). -/
68	inductive Out where
69	  | ok (d : DS)
70	  | fail
71	  | reject
72	
73	/-- The `n` cells of the stack from the index `b`. -/
74	def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n
75	
76	/-- The cells above the mark `m`, from its top to the current top: those that `rewind m` returns
77	to the available part (brief: "les régions au-dessus de `m`"). A region issued after `m` and still
78	below the top lies there, but not every such region does: a block grown after `m` from a base below
79	`m` starts below it, and a region issued after `m` and returned by an intermediate `rewind` lies
80	above the current top (`case_rewind_reading`; report, (f)). -/
81	def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := cellsOf st m.top (st.top - m.top)
82	
83	/-- The stack seen as an administration of its storage, for `MetaRightM` and `blockOf`. -/
84	def Stack.arena (st : Stack) : Arena := ⟨st.storage, st.internal, [], []⟩
85	
86	/-- No active authority is held by the destination (O8.2, §77.2). -/
87	def NoHeld (s : S3) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
88	  ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True
89	
90	instance (s : S3) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (NoHeld s dst) := by unfold NoHeld; infer_instance
91	
92	/-- Static preconditions of `push` of the cells `r`, checked before the room (§58, §77.4), those of
93	the restricted `issue` (`IssueStaticR`, §77.1 and §77.2): the stack is live, the current frame has
94	exercisable `Modify` on the stack value (`MetaRightM`), and the destination is a usable leaf under
95	exercisable `Modify`, not `Init`, holding no active authority and outside `r`. The inclusion of the
96	region in the storage is the room. -/
97	def PushStatic (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
98	  s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRightM s st.arena ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
99	    HasRight s .modify dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ NoHeld s dst ∧ dst ∉ r
100	
101	instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (PushStatic s st r dst) := by
102	  unfold PushStatic; infer_instance

104	/-- The derived `issue` (question 1, `issue_as_kernel_split`): `split` of `internal` on `r`, then
105	`store` of the block into `dst`. -/
106	def IssueSeq (k : K) (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
107	  SplitPre k s st.internal [r] ∧ StorePre (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena r)) s.A.length dst
108	
109	instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (s : S3) (st : Stack)
110	    (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (IssueSeq k s st r dst) := by
111	  unfold IssueSeq; infer_instance
112	
113	/-- Arrival state of the derived `issue`. -/
114	def issueSeqEff (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 :=
115	  storeEff (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena r)) s.A.length dst
116	
117	/-- The derived `reset` on the cells above `m` (question 1, `reset_as_kernel`): `split` of
118	`internal` on them, then `release` of the derived authority. -/
119	def RewindSeq (k : K) (s : S3) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop :=
120	  SplitPre k s st.internal [above st m] ∧
121	    ReleasePre (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena (above st m))) s.A.length
122	
123	instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (s : S3) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) :
124	    Decidable (RewindSeq k s st m) := by
125	  unfold RewindSeq; infer_instance

127	/-- The guard of §56 for `internal` `i`: no live arena and no live stack already uses it. -/
128	def Guard56 (d : DS) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
129	  (∀ ar ∈ d.s.arenas, d.s.Active ar.internal → ar.internal ≠ i) ∧
130	    ∀ x ∈ d.stacks, d.s.Active x.internal → x.internal ≠ i
131	
132	instance (d : DS) (i : Nat) : Decidable (Guard56 d i) := by unfold Guard56; infer_instance

134	section Ops
135	variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
136	  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
137	  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]
138	
139	/-- Creation of a stack on `storage` administered by `internal` (as O17, §76): the preconditions of
140	`newArena` and the guard of §56 on both registries, arenas and stacks. -/
141	def newStack (d : DS) (storage i : Nat) : Out :=
142	  if NewArenaPreNG d.s storage i ∧ Guard56 d i then
143	    .ok { d with stacks := d.stacks ++ [⟨storage, i, footprint d.s.P storage, 0, [], []⟩] }
144	  else .reject

146	/-- `push size dst` on the stack `j` (brief: "émission au sommet (`issue` restreint)"): the static
147	clauses of the restricted `issue` (`PushStatic`), then `fail` when fewer than `size` cells are left,
148	then the derived `issue` of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`. By `issue_as_kernel_split`, this
149	realisation through kernel steps differs from the restricted `issue` only by clause 5 of `store`
150	(O8.5), which it inherits. `size` may be zero: the block then has an empty footprint, as the
151	restricted `issue` of the empty region (`ce_empty_region`), and it blocks no `rewind`. -/
152	def push (d : DS) (j size dst : Nat) : Out :=
153	  match d.stacks[j]? with
154	  | none => .reject
155	  | some st =>
156	    if PushStatic d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
157	      if st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length then
158	        if IssueSeq k d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
159	          .ok { d with
160	            s := issueSeqEff d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst
161	            stacks := d.stacks.set j
162	              { st with
163	                top := st.top + size
164	                blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, d.s.A.length, dst⟩] } }
165	        else .reject
166	      else .fail
167	    else .reject

169	/-- `mark` on the stack `j` (brief): `ok`, a mark (stack, fresh identifier, top) appended to the
170	live marks. -/
171	def mark (d : DS) (j : Nat) : Out :=
172	  match d.stacks[j]? with
173	  | none => .reject
174	  | some st => .ok { d with
175	      stacks := d.stacks.set j { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, d.fresh, st.top⟩] }
176	      fresh := d.fresh + 1 }

178	/-- `rewind m` on the stack `j` (brief): `fail` when `m` is not a live mark of the stack; then the
179	derived `reset` on the cells above `m`, `split` of `internal` on them and `release`, which rejects
180	when an active authority derived from `internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`)
181	and also when the current frame cannot exercise `internal` at `Modify` (O2.1, the restricted
182	`MetaRight` of §78.1); `ok`: the top returns to the top of `m`, the blocks whose base is above it
183	are forgotten, `m` and the later marks are removed, the older marks stay (`rewind_removes`). A stack
184	that does not exist rejects (no stack value). -/
185	def rewind (d : DS) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) : Out :=
186	  match d.stacks[j]? with
187	  | none => .reject
188	  | some st =>
189	    if m ∈ st.marks then
190	      if RewindSeq k d.s st m then
191	        .ok { d with
192	          s := releaseEff (d.s.addAuth (blockOf d.s st.arena (above st m))) d.s.A.length
193	          stacks := d.stacks.set j
194	            { st with
195	              top := m.top
196	              blocks := st.blocks.filter (·.base < m.top)
197	              marks := st.marks.takeWhile (· ≠ m) } }
198	      else .reject
199	    else .fail

201	/-- `grow b extra` on the stack `j` (brief: in place only). Static clauses, checked before the room
202	(§58): `b` is the authority of the last block, at the top, `extra` is positive ("taille plus
203	grande"), `b` can be released, the stack is live and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` on
204	the stack value (`MetaRightM`). `fail` when fewer than `extra` cells follow the block; otherwise
205	`release` of `b`, then the derived `issue` of the region of the same base and of size `size + extra`
206	into the destination recorded for the block. That destination is `Init` (the first `store` wrote
207	it): the derived `issue` accepts it (O8.2), the restricted `issue` would not (§77.2, report (c)). -/
208	def grow (d : DS) (j b extra : Nat) : Out :=
209	  match d.stacks[j]? with
210	  | none => .reject
211	  | some st =>
212	    match st.blocks.getLast? with
213	    | none => .reject
214	    | some x =>
215	      if 0 < extra ∧ x.auth = b ∧ x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ ReleasePre d.s b ∧
216	          d.s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRightM d.s st.arena then
217	        if x.base + x.size + extra ≤ st.cells.length then
218	          if IssueSeq k (releaseEff d.s b) st (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst then
219	            .ok { d with
220	              s := issueSeqEff (releaseEff d.s b) st (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst
221	              stacks := d.stacks.set j
222	                { st with
223	                  top := x.base + x.size + extra
224	                  blocks := st.blocks.dropLast ++ [⟨x.base, x.size + extra, d.s.A.length, x.dst⟩] } }
225	          else .reject
226	        else .fail
227	      else .reject

229	/-- Operations of a run of the library: a kernel or arena step, or a stack operation. -/
230	inductive DOp where
231	  | kernel (o : Op)
232	  | newStack (storage i : Nat)
233	  | push (j size dst : Nat)
234	  | mark (j : Nat)
235	  | rewind (j : Nat) (m : Mark)
236	  | grow (j b extra : Nat)

238	/-- The guard of §56 that a kernel `newArena` adds in the library: the registry of the stacks. -/
239	def KGuard (d : DS) : Op → Prop
240	  | .newArena _ i => ∀ x ∈ d.stacks, d.s.Active x.internal → x.internal ≠ i
241	  | _ => True
242	
243	instance (d : DS) (o : Op) : Decidable (KGuard d o) := by
244	  cases o <;> unfold KGuard <;> infer_instance
245	
246	/-- A step of the library. A kernel `newArena` also consults the registry of the stacks (§56). -/
247	def dexec (d : DS) : DOp → Out
248	  | .kernel o =>
249	    if KGuard d o then
250	      match kexec k d.s o with
251	      | some s' => .ok { d with s := s' }
252	      | none => .reject
253	    else .reject
254	  | .newStack st i => DataStack.newStack d st i
255	  | .push j size dst => DataStack.push k d j size dst
256	  | .mark j => DataStack.mark d j
257	  | .rewind j m => DataStack.rewind k d j m
258	  | .grow j b extra => DataStack.grow k d j b extra
259	
260	/-- A run of the library: `some` of the final state when every step is `ok`. -/
261	def drun (d : DS) : List DOp → Option DS
262	  | [] => some d
263	  | o :: os =>
264	    match dexec k d o with
265	    | .ok d' => drun d' os
266	    | _ => none
267	
268	end Ops

378	/-- The derived `issue` is a `split` step then a `store` step of `Reachable` (O2, O8). -/
379	theorem issueSeq_reach {statics : Statics} {s : S3} {st : Stack} {r : List Nat} {dst : Nat}

381	    Reachable k statics (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena r)) ∧

403	/-- Every `ok` step of the library takes kernel steps of `Reachable` only. -/
404	theorem dexec_reach {statics : Statics} {d d' : DS} {o : DOp} (hr : Reachable k statics d.s)
405	    (h : dexec k d o = .ok d') : Reachable k statics d'.s := by
406	  cases o with
407	  | kernel o => exact reachable_step hr (kexec_step (dexec_kernel h).1)
408	  | newStack st i => obtain ⟨-, -, rfl⟩ := newStack_ok h; exact hr
409	  | push j size dst =>
410	    obtain ⟨st, -, -, -, hseq, rfl⟩ := push_ok h; exact (issueSeq_reach hr hseq).2
411	  | mark j => obtain ⟨st, -, rfl⟩ := mark_ok h; exact hr
412	  | rewind j m =>
413	    obtain ⟨st, -, -, ⟨hsp, hrel⟩, rfl⟩ := rewind_ok h
414	    have h1 : Reachable k statics (d.s.addAuth (blockOf d.s st.arena (above st m))) :=
415	      .split hr (rs := [above st m]) (src := st.internal) (.ok hsp)
416	    exact .release h1 (.ok hrel)
417	  | grow j b extra =>
418	    obtain ⟨st, x, -, -, -, -, -, hrel, -, -, hseq, rfl⟩ := grow_ok h
419	    exact (issueSeq_reach (.release hr (.ok hrel)) hseq).2
420	
421	theorem drun_reach {statics : Statics} : ∀ {d d' : DS} {os : List DOp},
422	    Reachable k statics d.s → drun k d os = some d' → Reachable k statics d'.s
423	  | d, d', [], hr, h => by simp only [drun, Option.some.injEq] at h; subst h; exact hr
424	  | d, d', o :: os, hr, h => by
425	    simp only [drun] at h
426	    split at h
427	    · rename_i d₁ h₁; exact drun_reach (dexec_reach hr h₁) h
428	    · cases h

502	/-- `rewind_rejects_live_above` (brief): `rewind m` of a live mark is rejected when an active
503	authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m` (`above`, the cells that the rewind
504	returns): its effective `Modify` on that cell is gone, so `split` of `internal` on the cells above
505	`m` is rejected (O2.1). The brief's "couvre une région émise après `m`" is read on the cells that the
506	rewind returns (`above`; report, (f)). -/

508	    (hst : d.stacks[j]? = some st) (hm : m ∈ st.marks) {x l : Nat} {y : Authority}
509	    (hy : d.s.A[x]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) (hx : st.internal ∈ d.s.ancs x)
510	    (hly : l ∈ y.footprint) (hl : l ∈ above st m) : rewind k d j m = .reject := by

512	    effective_ne_modify_of_active_desc hy ya hly hx (h.1.2.2.1 _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl)

591	  intro l hl

611	/-- The marks of the stack `i` are pairwise distinct, name the stack `i` and have identifiers below
612	`fresh`. -/
613	def MarksWF (d : DS) : Prop :=
614	  ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), d.stacks[i]? = some st →
615	    st.marks.Nodup ∧ ∀ m ∈ st.marks, m.stack = i ∧ m.id < d.fresh

617	/-- The mark `m` is live in no stack, and its identifier was given out. -/
618	def Gone (d : DS) (m : Mark) : Prop :=
619	  m.id < d.fresh ∧ ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), d.stacks[i]? = some st → m ∉ st.marks

621	theorem marksWF_init : MarksWF DS.init := fun i st h => by simp [DS.init] at h

632	    (hQ : ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), d.stacks[i]? = some st → ∀ m ∈ st.marks, Q i m) {i : Nat}
633	    {st'' : Stack} (h : (d.stacks.set j st')[i]? = some st'') (hm : ∀ m ∈ st'.marks, m ∈ st.marks) :
634	    ∀ m ∈ st''.marks, Q i m := by
635	  intro m hm'
636	  rcases getElem?_set_cases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩

650	  have hQ : ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), d.stacks[i]? = some st → ∀ m' ∈ st.marks, m' ≠ m :=
651	    fun i st h m' hm' e => hno i st h (e ▸ hm')
652	  have fin : ∀ {l : List Stack}, (∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), l[i]? = some st → ∀ m' ∈ st.marks, m' ≠ m) →
653	      ∀ (i : Nat) (st : Stack), l[i]? = some st → m ∉ st.marks := fun hl i st h hm => hl i st h m hm rfl
654	  cases o with
655	  | kernel o =>
656	    obtain ⟨-, hs, hf⟩ := dexec_kernel h
657	    exact ⟨by rw [hf]; exact hid, fun i st h' hm => hno i st (by rw [← hs]; exact h') hm⟩
658	  | newStack st i =>
659	    obtain ⟨-, -, rfl⟩ := newStack_ok h
660	    refine ⟨hid, fun i' st' h' hm => ?_⟩
661	    rcases getElem?_append_single h' with h' | ⟨-, rfl⟩
662	    · exact hno i' st' h' hm
663	    · simp at hm
664	  | push j size dst =>

671	    rcases getElem?_set_cases h' with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩
672	    · rcases List.mem_append.1 hm with hm | hm
673	      · exact hno _ st hst hm
674	      · rw [List.mem_singleton] at hm; rw [hm] at hid; exact Nat.lt_irrefl _ hid

679	    intro i st'' h' m' hm'
680	    exact stacks_set_marks hst hQ h' (fun _ h => List.takeWhile_subset _ h) m' hm'
681	  | grow j b extra =>
682	    obtain ⟨st, x, hst, -, -, -, -, -, -, -, -, rfl⟩ := grow_ok h

726	        ⟨((hw i st' h').2 m hm).1, Nat.lt_succ_of_lt ((hw i st' h').2 m hm).2⟩⟩

741	  | d, d', o :: os, h, hw => by
742	    simp only [drun] at h

750	/-- Under `MarksWF`, `rewind m` keeps exactly the marks older than `m` and removes `m` and every later
751	mark of the stack (brief: "`m` et toutes les marques au-dessus sont retirées, les plus anciennes
752	restent vivantes"). -/
753	theorem rewind_removes {d d' : DS} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} (hw : MarksWF d)
754	    (h : rewind k d j m = .ok d') {st : Stack} (hst : d.stacks[j]? = some st)
755	    {pre post : List Mark} (hs : st.marks = pre ++ m :: post) :
756	    ∃ st', d'.stacks[j]? = some st' ∧ st'.marks = pre ∧ ∀ m' ∈ m :: post, m' ∉ st'.marks := by
757	  have hnd := (hw j st hst).1
758	  rw [hs] at hnd
759	  have hdisj := (List.nodup_append.1 hnd).2.2
760	  have hmpre : m ∉ pre := fun h => hdisj m h m (List.mem_cons_self ..) rfl
761	  obtain ⟨⟨st', hst', hpre, -⟩, -, -⟩ := rewind_keeps_older_marks h hst hs hmpre
762	  exact ⟨st', hst', hpre, fun m' hm' hin => hdisj m' (hpre ▸ hin) m' hm' rfl⟩
763	
764	/-- `mark_no_aba` (brief): every mark that `rewind m` removes, `m` and the later marks of the stack,
765	is live in no stack in any later state, even when the top returns to the same position: identifiers
766	are fresh and a mark is live by membership, so `rewind` of a removed mark fails forever after. -/
767	theorem mark_no_aba {d d₁ d' : DS} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} {os : List DOp} (hw : MarksWF d)
768	    (hr : rewind k d j m = .ok d₁) (h : drun k d₁ os = some d') {st : Stack}
769	    (hst : d.stacks[j]? = some st) {pre post : List Mark} (hs : st.marks = pre ++ m :: post)
770	    {m' : Mark} (hm' : m' ∈ m :: post) :
771	    (∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), d'.stacks[i]? = some st' → m' ∉ st'.marks) ∧
772	      ∀ st', d'.stacks[j]? = some st' → rewind k d' j m' = .fail := by
773	  obtain ⟨st₁, hst₁, hgone1, hgone⟩ :
774	      ∃ st₁, d₁.stacks[j]? = some st₁ ∧ st₁.marks = pre ∧ ∀ m' ∈ m :: post, m' ∉ st₁.marks :=
775	    rewind_removes hw hr hst hs
776	  obtain ⟨st₀, hst₀, -, -, rfl⟩ := rewind_ok hr
777	  rw [hst] at hst₀; cases hst₀
778	  have hm'st : m' ∈ st.marks := by rw [hs]; exact List.mem_append_right _ hm'
779	  obtain ⟨-, hwj⟩ := hw j st hst
780	  have hg : Gone { d with
781	      s := releaseEff (d.s.addAuth (blockOf d.s st.arena (above st m))) d.s.A.length
782	      stacks := d.stacks.set j
783	        { st with
784	          top := m.top
785	          blocks := st.blocks.filter (·.base < m.top)
786	          marks := st.marks.takeWhile (· ≠ m) } } m' := by
787	    refine ⟨(hwj m' hm'st).2, fun i st' h' hm'' => ?_⟩
788	    rcases getElem?_set_cases h' with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨hi, h'⟩
789	    · rw [hst₁] at h'; cases h'; exact hgone m' hm' hm''
790	    · exact hi (((hw i st' h').2 m' hm'').1.symm.trans (hwj m' hm'st).1)
791	  have hg' := drun_gone h hg
792	  refine ⟨hg'.2, fun st' hst' => ?_⟩
793	  simp [rewind, hst', hg'.2 j st' hst']

796	applies to it. -/
797	theorem drun_init_marksWF {os : List DOp} {d : DS} (h : drun k DS.init os = some d) : MarksWF d :=
798	  drun_marksWF h marksWF_init

805	/-! ## Bytes of the prefix after `grow` (refinement `Ern.MM23`) -/
806	
807	/-- The state after the release of `b` and the `split` of `grow`, before the `store`. -/
808	def growMid (s : S3) (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (b extra : Nat) : S3 :=
809	  (releaseEff s b).addAuth (blockOf (releaseEff s b) st.arena (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)))
810	
811	/-- `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` (brief), through the refinement `Ern.MM23` unchanged: in a reached
812	state, the `ok` of `grow` is a `release` and a `split`, steps without an MM-02 step (`NoStep`, K4,
813	whose arrival states stay in `Repr` with the same MM-02 state, `r6_noStep`), then a `store`, whose
814	MM-02 counterpart is one write of the range of the destination (`storeOps`, L6, `r6_store`); for
815	every layout well-formed in the state (`LayoutWF`), that write leaves the bytes of every cell of the
816	old block, values and provenances (`rangeBytes`), unchanged. Under `DDSound k`. -/
817	theorem grow_keeps_prefix_bytes (hdd : DDSound k) {statics : Statics} {d d' : DS} {j b extra : Nat}
818	    (hr : Reachable k statics d.s) (h : grow k d j b extra = .ok d') {st : Stack} {x : Blk}
819	    (hst : d.stacks[j]? = some st) (hx : st.blocks.getLast? = some x) {L : MM23.Layout}
820	    {s2 : MM02.State} (hlw : MM23.LayoutWF L d.s s2) (pe : MM23.PtrEnc) :
821	    MM23.NoStep k d.s (releaseEff d.s b) ∧
822	      MM23.NoStep k (releaseEff d.s b) (growMid d.s st x b extra) ∧
823	      StoreStep (releaseEff d.s b).A.length x.dst (growMid d.s st x b extra) (.ok d'.s) ∧
824	      ∀ l ∈ cellsOf st x.base x.size,
825	        MM23.rangeBytes (MM23.exec s2 (MM23.storeOps pe s2 L (growMid d.s st x b extra)
826	          (releaseEff d.s b).A.length x.dst)) L l = MM23.rangeBytes s2 L l := by
827	  obtain ⟨st₀, x₀, hst₀, hx₀, -, -, -, hrel, -, -, ⟨hsp, hstore⟩, rfl⟩ := grow_ok h
828	  rw [hst] at hst₀; cases hst₀; rw [hx] at hx₀; cases hx₀
829	  have hr₁ : Reachable k statics (releaseEff d.s b) := .release hr (.ok hrel)
830	  have hr₂ : Reachable k statics (growMid d.s st x b extra) :=
831	    .split hr₁ (rs := [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]) (src := st.internal) (.ok hsp)
832	  refine ⟨.release (.ok hrel), .split (rs := [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)])
833	    (src := st.internal) (.ok hsp), .ok hstore, fun l hl => ?_⟩
834	  have hy₀ := addAuth_self (releaseEff d.s b)
835	    (blockOf (releaseEff d.s b) st.arena (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)))
836	  have hP : (growMid d.s st x b extra).P = d.s.P := releaseEff_P d.s b
837	  obtain ⟨-, hu, -, hcov, -, hleaf, -, -, -⟩ := hstore
838	  have hlr' : l ∈ cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra) := (cellsOf_prefix st x.base x.size extra).subset hl
839	  have hlr : l ∈ (growMid d.s st x b extra).afp (releaseEff d.s b).A.length := by
840	    simp only [growMid, S3.afp, hy₀]; exact hlr'
841	  have hne : l ≠ x.dst := by
842	    intro he; rw [he] at hlr
843	    exact (hcov x.dst hlr).1 (mem_footprint.2 ⟨hu.lt, hleaf, hu.lt, .inl rfl⟩)
844	  have hfp := (MM23.reachable_fpLeaves_frameOwnedLive hdd hr₂).1
845	  have hwf₂ := (reachable_invariants hdd hr₂).1
846	  have hll : isLeaf d.s.P l := by rw [← hP]; exact hfp _ _ hy₀ l hlr'
847	  have hlt : l < d.s.P.length := by rw [← hP]; exact hwf₂.2.1 _ _ hy₀ l hlr'
848	  have hdl : x.dst < d.s.P.length := by rw [← hP]; exact hu.lt
849	  have hdleaf : isLeaf d.s.P x.dst := by rw [← hP]; exact hleaf
850	  have halloc : MM23.AllocP s2 (L x.dst).alloc fun _ => True :=
851	    (hlw.within x.dst hdl hdleaf).mono fun _ _ => trivial
852	  have hdis : (L l).alloc ≠ (L x.dst).alloc ∨
853	      MM02.RangeDisjoint (L l).off (L l).len (L x.dst).off (L x.dst).len := by
854	    by_cases ha : (L l).alloc = (L x.dst).alloc
855	    · exact .inr (hlw.disjoint l hlt x.dst hdl hll hdleaf hne ha)
856	    · exact .inl ha
857	  exact MM23.rangeBytes_write_other (MM23.Dom.refl s2) halloc hdis
858

861	/-! ## Cases (brief, question 2)
862	
863	Runs from `DS.init` under the test contracts `K0`; each statement includes that the run is `ok`
864	(`isSome`), so that `final` is its state; every verdict by `decide`. -/
865	
866	def Out.isOk : Out → Bool
867	  | .ok _ => true
868	  | _ => false
869	
870	def Out.isFail : Out → Bool
871	  | .fail => true
872	  | _ => false
873	
874	def Out.isReject : Out → Bool
875	  | .reject => true
876	  | _ => false

878	/-- The state of a run from `DS.init` (`DS.init` when a step is not `ok`). -/
879	def final (os : List DOp) : DS := (drun K0 DS.init os).getD DS.init
880	
881	/-- The kernel state of an `ok` run of the library is reached. -/
882	theorem final_reach {os : List DOp} (h : (drun K0 DS.init os).isSome = true) :
883	    Reachable K0 [] (final os).s := by
884	  obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := Option.isSome_iff_exists.1 h
885	  have := drun_reach (statics := []) (show Reachable K0 [] DS.init.s from .init (by decide)) hd
886	  simp only [final, hd, Option.getD_some]; exact this
887	
888	/-- A cell of the storage `p`. -/
889	abbrev cellOf (p : Nat) : Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat := (some p, none, 0)
890	
891	/-- One stack: frame 1 with the leaves 0 (stack value), 2, 3, 4 (cells of the storage 1), 5, 6, 7
892	(destinations), of root authorities 0 (on 0), 1 (on 1), 2, 3, 4 (on 5, 6, 7); `internal` 5 derived
893	from 1 and stored into 0; the stack 0 created on 1 with `internal` 5. -/
894	def setup1 : List DOp :=
895	  [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, cellOf 1, cellOf 1, cellOf 1, lf, lf, lf]),
896	    .kernel (.derive 1 1 .modify), .kernel (.store 5 0), .newStack 1 5]
897	
898	/-- Mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩`, `push 2` into 5 (block 6 on `[2, 3]`), mark `⟨0, 1, 2⟩`, `push 1` into 6
899	(block 7 on `[4]`). -/
900	def opsR : List DOp := setup1 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 2 5, .mark 0, .push 0 1 6]
901	
902	/-- **`rewind` refused then accepted**: `rewind ⟨0, 1, 2⟩` is rejected while the block 7, derived

906	    (drun K0 DS.init opsR).isSome = true ∧

940	/-- Two stacks: frame 1 with the leaves 0 and 8 (stack values), the storages 1 (cells 2, 3, 4)
941	and 9 (cells 10, 11), the destinations 5, 6, 7, 12, of root authorities 0 to 7; `internal` 8 on 1
942	stored into 0, stack 0; `internal` 9 on 9 stored into 8, stack 1. -/
943	def setup2 : List DOp :=

951	`newArena` with `internal` 8, which the kernel alone accepts; each stack has its top, blocks and
952	marks; `rewind` of stack 0 to its mark is rejected while its block 10 lives, a mark of stack 1 is not
953	a live mark of stack 0 (`fail`), stack 1 rewinds to its mark and pushes again. -/
954	theorem case_stacks :
955	    (drun K0 DS.init setup2).isSome = true ∧
956	    (dexec K0 (final setup2) (.newStack 1 8)).isReject = true ∧
957	    (kexec K0 (final setup2).s (.newArena 1 8)).isSome = true ∧
958	    (dexec K0 (final setup2) (.kernel (.newArena 1 8))).isReject = true ∧
959	    (drun K0 DS.init opsS).isSome = true ∧
960	    (final opsS).stacks.map (fun st => (st.internal, st.top, st.blocks, st.marks)) =
961	      [(8, 1, [⟨0, 1, 10, 5⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩]), (9, 1, [⟨0, 1, 11, 12⟩], [⟨1, 1, 1⟩])] ∧

963	    (dexec K0 (final opsS) (.rewind 0 ⟨1, 1, 1⟩)).isFail = true ∧
964	    (drun K0 DS.init (opsS ++ [.rewind 1 ⟨1, 1, 1⟩, .push 1 1 6])).isSome = true := by

967	/-- Frame use: the caller derives 6 from the root of the stack value at `Modify` and passes it to a
968	callee with one local 8; the callee marks the stack at entry and pushes 2 cells into its local
969	(block 8). At exit, `rewind` is rejected while the block lives; after `endUse` of the local, which
970	releases the block, `rewind` to the entry mark and `exitFrame` are accepted, and the stack is empty
971	again. -/
972	def opsF : List DOp :=
973	  setup1 ++ [.kernel (.derive 0 0 .modify), .kernel (.enter [6] [lf]), .mark 0, .push 0 2 8]
974	
975	theorem case_frame :
976	    (drun K0 DS.init opsF).isSome = true ∧
977	    (dexec K0 (final opsF) (.rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩)).isReject = true ∧
978	    (drun K0 DS.init (opsF ++ [.kernel (.endUse 8), .rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩, .kernel .exit])).isSome = true ∧
979	    (final (opsF ++ [.kernel (.endUse 8), .rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩, .kernel .exit])).stacks.map
980	      (fun st => (st.top, st.blocks, st.marks)) = [(0, [], [])] := by
981	  decide

983	/-- Block 6 pushed on `[2, 3]`, mark `⟨0, 0, 2⟩`, block grown to `[2, 3, 4]` (authority 7), released;
984	then 8 derived from `internal` 5 on the cell 2, below the mark. -/
985	def opsE4 : List DOp :=
986	  setup1 ++ [.push 0 2 5, .mark 0, .grow 0 6 1, .kernel (.release 7), .kernel (.derive 5 2 .modify)]
987	
988	/-- Marks `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` and `⟨0, 1, 1⟩` around block 6 on `[2]`; block 7 on `[3]` pushed after both
989	marks, released, and returned by `rewind ⟨0, 1, 1⟩`; block 6 released; then 9 derived from

991	def opsE8 : List DOp :=
992	  setup1 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 1 5, .mark 0, .push 0 1 6, .kernel (.release 7),
993	    .rewind 0 ⟨0, 1, 1⟩, .kernel (.release 6), .kernel (.derive 5 3 .modify)]
994	
995	/-- Mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩`, then a `push` of size 0: block 6, active, of empty footprint. -/
996	def opsE3 : List DOp := setup1 ++ [.mark 0, .push 0 0 5]

999	the cells it returns (`above`). In `opsE4` the authority 8, active and derived from `internal`,
1000	covers the cell 2 of the region `[2, 3, 4]` issued (by `grow`) after the mark `⟨0, 0, 2⟩`, below

1002	the cell 3 of a region issued after `⟨0, 0, 0⟩`, now above the top, and `rewind` is accepted (the
1003	cell 3 is already available). In `opsE3` the empty block 6, issued after the mark and active, does
1004	not block `rewind`, and stays active once the metadata forget it. -/
1005	theorem case_rewind_reading :
1006	    (drun K0 DS.init opsE4).isSome = true ∧
1007	    (final opsE4).s.A[8]?.map (fun y => (y.active, y.origin, y.footprint)) = some (true, some 5, [2]) ∧
1008	    (dexec K0 (final opsE4) (.rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 2⟩)).isOk = true ∧
1009	    (drun K0 DS.init opsE8).isSome = true ∧
1010	    (final opsE8).s.A[9]?.map (fun y => (y.active, y.origin, y.footprint)) = some (true, some 5, [3]) ∧
1011	    (dexec K0 (final opsE8) (.rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩)).isOk = true ∧
1012	    (drun K0 DS.init (opsE3 ++ [.rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩])).isSome = true ∧
1013	    (final (opsE3 ++ [.rewind 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩])).s.A[6]?.map (fun y => (y.active, y.origin, y.footprint)) =
1014	      some (true, some 5, []) := by

1016	
1017	/-- Block 6 pushed into 5, then a callee entered with only 7, a `Modify` derived from the root of 5:

1029	    (drun K0 DS.init (setup1 ++ [.kernel (.write 2 [5])])).isSome = true ∧

1033	    (dexec K0 (final setup1) (.push 0 4 5)).isFail = true := by

4	/-!
5	# DataStack, a library instance over the kernel (derivability pass 0.1, question 2)
6	
7	A stack administers a storage through an authority `internal` held by the stack value, as an arena
8	does (candidate Spec 1 §36, §46), with library metadata: the ordered leaves of the storage, the
9	top, the issued blocks and the live marks. Its operations are built on kernel steps and on the
10	derived `issue` and `reset` of question 1 (`Ern.Derived.Arena`):
11	
12	* `push`: the restricted `issue` at the top, its static clauses (§77.1, §77.2) checked before the
13	  room, realised by `split` of `internal` on the cells then `store` of the block into the
14	  destination; `fail` when no room is left;
15	* `mark`: a mark (stack, fresh identifier, top), metadata only;
16	* `rewind`: the derived `reset` on the cells above the mark, `split` of `internal` on them then
17	  `release` of the derived authority; `fail` for a mark that is not live in the stack;
18	* `grow`: in place, `release` of the last block, then the derived `issue` of a region of the same
19	  base and of larger size into the same destination, which is `Init`; `fail` when no room is left.
20	
21	Every `ok` step of the library takes kernel steps of `Reachable` only (`dexec_reach`). The theorems
22	of the brief are `rewind_rejects_live_above`, `mark_no_aba` (with `rewind_removes`),
23	`rewind_keeps_older_marks`,
24	`grow_same_base`, `grow_keeps_prefix_init` and `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` (through the refinement
25	`Ern.MM23`, unchanged). The decisions the brief does not settle are listed in the report
26	(`formal/reports/Derivability_v0.1.md`, (c) and (f)).
27	-/
28	
29	namespace Ern.Lib.DataStack
30	
31	open Ern.MM03 Ern.HandlePool Ern.MM03.Horrors Ern.Derived.Arena
32	
33	/-- A block issued by a stack: base and size in the cells of the stack, authority, destination. -/
34	structure Blk where
35	  base : Nat
36	  size : Nat
37	  auth : Nat
38	  dst : Nat
39	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
40	
41	/-- A mark (brief: "(pile, identifiant frais, sommet)"). -/
42	structure Mark where
43	  stack : Nat
44	  id : Nat
45	  top : Nat
46	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
47	
48	/-- A stack (brief: "stockage, `internal`, sommet, liste ordonnée des marques vivantes"); `cells`
49	are the ordered leaves of the storage, its footprint at creation; `blocks` the issued blocks,
50	oldest first. The stack value is the holder of `internal`. -/
51	structure Stack where
52	  storage : Nat
53	  internal : Nat
54	  cells : List Nat
55	  top : Nat
56	  blocks : List Blk
57	  marks : List Mark
58	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
59	
60	/-- State of the library: the kernel state, the stacks (the identity of a stack is its index) and
61	the next fresh mark identifier. -/
62	structure DS where
63	  s : S3
64	  stacks : List Stack
65	  fresh : Nat
66	
67	/-- Outcome of a library operation; `fail` leaves the state unchanged (§58). -/
68	inductive Out where
69	  | ok (d : DS)
70	  | fail
71	  | reject
72	
73	/-- The `n` cells of the stack from the index `b`. -/
74	def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n
75	
76	/-- The cells above the mark `m`, from its top to the current top: those that `rewind m` returns
77	to the available part (brief: "les régions au-dessus de `m`"). A region issued after `m` and still
78	below the top lies there, but not every such region does: a block grown after `m` from a base below
79	`m` starts below it, and a region issued after `m` and returned by an intermediate `rewind` lies
80	above the current top (`case_rewind_reading`; report, (f)). -/
81	def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := cellsOf st m.top (st.top - m.top)
82	
83	/-- The stack seen as an administration of its storage, for `MetaRightM` and `blockOf`. -/
84	def Stack.arena (st : Stack) : Arena := ⟨st.storage, st.internal, [], []⟩
85	
86	/-- No active authority is held by the destination (O8.2, §77.2). -/
87	def NoHeld (s : S3) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
88	  ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True
89	
90	instance (s : S3) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (NoHeld s dst) := by unfold NoHeld; infer_instance
91	
92	/-- Static preconditions of `push` of the cells `r`, checked before the room (§58, §77.4), those of
93	the restricted `issue` (`IssueStaticR`, §77.1 and §77.2): the stack is live, the current frame has
94	exercisable `Modify` on the stack value (`MetaRightM`), and the destination is a usable leaf under
95	exercisable `Modify`, not `Init`, holding no active authority and outside `r`. The inclusion of the
96	region in the storage is the room. -/
97	def PushStatic (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
98	  s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRightM s st.arena ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
99	    HasRight s .modify dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ NoHeld s dst ∧ dst ∉ r
100	
101	instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (PushStatic s st r dst) := by
102	  unfold PushStatic; infer_instance
103	
104	/-- The derived `issue` (question 1, `issue_as_kernel_split`): `split` of `internal` on `r`, then
105	`store` of the block into `dst`. -/
106	def IssueSeq (k : K) (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
107	  SplitPre k s st.internal [r] ∧ StorePre (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena r)) s.A.length dst
108	
109	instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (s : S3) (st : Stack)
110	    (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (IssueSeq k s st r dst) := by
111	  unfold IssueSeq; infer_instance
112	
113	/-- Arrival state of the derived `issue`. -/
114	def issueSeqEff (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 :=
115	  storeEff (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena r)) s.A.length dst
116	
117	/-- The derived `reset` on the cells above `m` (question 1, `reset_as_kernel`): `split` of
118	`internal` on them, then `release` of the derived authority. -/
119	def RewindSeq (k : K) (s : S3) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop :=
120	  SplitPre k s st.internal [above st m] ∧
121	    ReleasePre (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena (above st m))) s.A.length
122	
123	instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (s : S3) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) :
124	    Decidable (RewindSeq k s st m) := by
125	  unfold RewindSeq; infer_instance
126	
127	/-- The guard of §56 for `internal` `i`: no live arena and no live stack already uses it. -/
128	def Guard56 (d : DS) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
129	  (∀ ar ∈ d.s.arenas, d.s.Active ar.internal → ar.internal ≠ i) ∧
130	    ∀ x ∈ d.stacks, d.s.Active x.internal → x.internal ≠ i
131	
132	instance (d : DS) (i : Nat) : Decidable (Guard56 d i) := by unfold Guard56; infer_instance
133	
134	section Ops
135	variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
136	  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
137	  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]
138	
139	/-- Creation of a stack on `storage` administered by `internal` (as O17, §76): the preconditions of
140	`newArena` and the guard of §56 on both registries, arenas and stacks. -/
141	def newStack (d : DS) (storage i : Nat) : Out :=
142	  if NewArenaPreNG d.s storage i ∧ Guard56 d i then
143	    .ok { d with stacks := d.stacks ++ [⟨storage, i, footprint d.s.P storage, 0, [], []⟩] }
144	  else .reject
145	
146	/-- `push size dst` on the stack `j` (brief: "émission au sommet (`issue` restreint)"): the static
147	clauses of the restricted `issue` (`PushStatic`), then `fail` when fewer than `size` cells are left,
148	then the derived `issue` of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`. By `issue_as_kernel_split`, this
149	realisation through kernel steps differs from the restricted `issue` only by clause 5 of `store`
150	(O8.5), which it inherits. `size` may be zero: the block then has an empty footprint, as the
151	restricted `issue` of the empty region (`ce_empty_region`), and it blocks no `rewind`. -/
152	def push (d : DS) (j size dst : Nat) : Out :=
153	  match d.stacks[j]? with
154	  | none => .reject
155	  | some st =>
156	    if PushStatic d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
157	      if st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length then
158	        if IssueSeq k d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
159	          .ok { d with
160	            s := issueSeqEff d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst
161	            stacks := d.stacks.set j
162	              { st with
163	                top := st.top + size
164	                blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, d.s.A.length, dst⟩] } }
165	        else .reject
166	      else .fail
167	    else .reject
168	
169	/-- `mark` on the stack `j` (brief): `ok`, a mark (stack, fresh identifier, top) appended to the
170	live marks. -/
171	def mark (d : DS) (j : Nat) : Out :=
172	  match d.stacks[j]? with
173	  | none => .reject
174	  | some st => .ok { d with
175	      stacks := d.stacks.set j { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, d.fresh, st.top⟩] }
176	      fresh := d.fresh + 1 }
177	
178	/-- `rewind m` on the stack `j` (brief): `fail` when `m` is not a live mark of the stack; then the
179	derived `reset` on the cells above `m`, `split` of `internal` on them and `release`, which rejects
180	when an active authority derived from `internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`)
181	and also when the current frame cannot exercise `internal` at `Modify` (O2.1, the restricted
182	`MetaRight` of §78.1); `ok`: the top returns to the top of `m`, the blocks whose base is above it
183	are forgotten, `m` and the later marks are removed, the older marks stay (`rewind_removes`). A stack
184	that does not exist rejects (no stack value). -/
185	def rewind (d : DS) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) : Out :=
186	  match d.stacks[j]? with
187	  | none => .reject
188	  | some st =>
189	    if m ∈ st.marks then
190	      if RewindSeq k d.s st m then
191	        .ok { d with
192	          s := releaseEff (d.s.addAuth (blockOf d.s st.arena (above st m))) d.s.A.length
193	          stacks := d.stacks.set j
194	            { st with
195	              top := m.top
196	              blocks := st.blocks.filter (·.base < m.top)
197	              marks := st.marks.takeWhile (· ≠ m) } }
198	      else .reject
199	    else .fail
200	
201	/-- `grow b extra` on the stack `j` (brief: in place only). Static clauses, checked before the room
202	(§58): `b` is the authority of the last block, at the top, `extra` is positive ("taille plus
203	grande"), `b` can be released, the stack is live and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` on
204	the stack value (`MetaRightM`). `fail` when fewer than `extra` cells follow the block; otherwise
205	`release` of `b`, then the derived `issue` of the region of the same base and of size `size + extra`
206	into the destination recorded for the block. That destination is `Init` (the first `store` wrote
207	it): the derived `issue` accepts it (O8.2), the restricted `issue` would not (§77.2, report (c)). -/
208	def grow (d : DS) (j b extra : Nat) : Out :=
209	  match d.stacks[j]? with
210	  | none => .reject
211	  | some st =>
212	    match st.blocks.getLast? with
213	    | none => .reject
214	    | some x =>
215	      if 0 < extra ∧ x.auth = b ∧ x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ ReleasePre d.s b ∧
216	          d.s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRightM d.s st.arena then
217	        if x.base + x.size + extra ≤ st.cells.length then
218	          if IssueSeq k (releaseEff d.s b) st (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst then
219	            .ok { d with
220	              s := issueSeqEff (releaseEff d.s b) st (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst
221	              stacks := d.stacks.set j
222	                { st with
223	                  top := x.base + x.size + extra
224	                  blocks := st.blocks.dropLast ++ [⟨x.base, x.size + extra, d.s.A.length, x.dst⟩] } }
225	          else .reject
226	        else .fail
227	      else .reject

229	/-- Operations of a run of the library: a kernel or arena step, or a stack operation. -/
230	inductive DOp where
231	  | kernel (o : Op)
232	  | newStack (storage i : Nat)
233	  | push (j size dst : Nat)
234	  | mark (j : Nat)
235	  | rewind (j : Nat) (m : Mark)
236	  | grow (j b extra : Nat)

238	/-- The guard of §56 that a kernel `newArena` adds in the library: the registry of the stacks. -/
239	def KGuard (d : DS) : Op → Prop
240	  | .newArena _ i => ∀ x ∈ d.stacks, d.s.Active x.internal → x.internal ≠ i
241	  | _ => True
242	
243	instance (d : DS) (o : Op) : Decidable (KGuard d o) := by
244	  cases o <;> unfold KGuard <;> infer_instance
245	
246	/-- A step of the library. A kernel `newArena` also consults the registry of the stacks (§56). -/
247	def dexec (d : DS) : DOp → Out
248	  | .kernel o =>
249	    if KGuard d o then
250	      match kexec k d.s o with
251	      | some s' => .ok { d with s := s' }
252	      | none => .reject
253	    else .reject
254	  | .newStack st i => DataStack.newStack d st i
255	  | .push j size dst => DataStack.push k d j size dst
256	  | .mark j => DataStack.mark d j
257	  | .rewind j m => DataStack.rewind k d j m
258	  | .grow j b extra => DataStack.grow k d j b extra
259	
260	/-- A run of the library: `some` of the final state when every step is `ok`. -/
261	def drun (d : DS) : List DOp → Option DS
262	  | [] => some d
263	  | o :: os =>
264	    match dexec k d o with
265	    | .ok d' => drun d' os
266	    | _ => none
267	
268	end Ops

403	/-- Every `ok` step of the library takes kernel steps of `Reachable` only. -/
404	theorem dexec_reach {statics : Statics} {d d' : DS} {o : DOp} (hr : Reachable k statics d.s)
405	    (h : dexec k d o = .ok d') : Reachable k statics d'.s := by
406	  cases o with
407	  | kernel o => exact reachable_step hr (kexec_step (dexec_kernel h).1)
408	  | newStack st i => obtain ⟨-, -, rfl⟩ := newStack_ok h; exact hr
409	  | push j size dst =>
410	    obtain ⟨st, -, -, -, hseq, rfl⟩ := push_ok h; exact (issueSeq_reach hr hseq).2
411	  | mark j => obtain ⟨st, -, rfl⟩ := mark_ok h; exact hr
412	  | rewind j m =>
413	    obtain ⟨st, -, -, ⟨hsp, hrel⟩, rfl⟩ := rewind_ok h
414	    have h1 : Reachable k statics (d.s.addAuth (blockOf d.s st.arena (above st m))) :=
415	      .split hr (rs := [above st m]) (src := st.internal) (.ok hsp)
416	    exact .release h1 (.ok hrel)
417	  | grow j b extra =>
418	    obtain ⟨st, x, -, -, -, -, -, hrel, -, -, hseq, rfl⟩ := grow_ok h
419	    exact (issueSeq_reach (.release hr (.ok hrel)) hseq).2
